blockMcqs.question: You need exact COUNT(DISTINCT) for monthly billing. Which tool?
options: HyperLogLog for the speed
A Bloom filter on user IDs
A real set or database — no approximation
Count-Min sketch with wide rows
blockMcqs.explanation: Billing demands exactness; probabilistic structures trade accuracy for memory.

blockMcqs.question: Why prefer MurmurHash3 over SHA-256 in these structures?
options: SHA-256 produces too few output bits
Crypto security is wasted; you want speed and spread
MurmurHash3 guarantees zero collisions
SHA-256 is not deterministic across machines
blockMcqs.explanation: These need uniform, fast hashing; collision-resistance only costs throughput.

blockMcqs.question: Going from N to N+1 nodes, why is hash-mod-N catastrophic for a cache?
options: The hash function must be recomputed entirely
The modulus shifts, remapping nearly every key at once
Each key gets two owners instead of one
Adding a node halves the hash range
blockMcqs.explanation: Changing N changes the slot for almost all keys, triggering a miss storm.

blockMcqs.question: What happens on the ring when a node dies and there are no vnodes?
options: Its entire load dumps onto one clockwise neighbor
All keys are evenly redistributed across every node
The ring shrinks and rehashes globally
Only the dead node's replicas are affected
blockMcqs.explanation: A single ring position means one neighbor absorbs the whole arc — a hotspot.

blockMcqs.question: A Bloom filter query returns all bits set. What can you conclude?
options: The item is definitely in the set
The item is probably present; could be a false positive
The item was definitely never added
The filter is full and must be resized
blockMcqs.explanation: Other items' bits can collectively set those positions, so all-ones is only 'maybe'.

blockMcqs.question: Why does a Count-Min sketch take the minimum across rows?
options: The minimum averages out random noise
It is the least-polluted estimate and never undercounts
Rows store different items, so min finds the match
The minimum corrects for false negatives
blockMcqs.explanation: Collisions only inflate counters, so the smallest is closest to the true count.

blockMcqs.question: How do you merge two HyperLogLog sketches for a global distinct count?
options: Add the two estimated counts together
Average the per-bucket values
Take the per-bucket maximum, then estimate
Concatenate the bucket arrays
blockMcqs.explanation: Adding counts double-counts shared items; per-bucket max preserves the longest runs.

blockMcqs.question: Adding more hash functions to a Bloom filter will:
options: Always lower the false-positive rate
Help only up to an optimum, then raise it
Have no effect on false positives
Eliminate false positives entirely
blockMcqs.explanation: Optimal k is (m/n)·ln2; too many hashes fill the array and worsen FP.
